# Independent audit: globally deepest five-rectangle inside-facet obstruction

Source: `candidate 79b44436a463e3c4`.

Certificate: `supporting computation globally_deepest_rectangle_inside_facets_certificate_two_sided.json`.



The supplied verifier was read in full and rerun: **1,529 exact checks PASS**. I also wrote and ran the independent verifier `supporting computation verify_global_rectangle_inside_certificate_audit_slab_recovery.py`: **16,346 exact checks PASS**. It reads the saved certificate and does not use the generator's polygon clipping or fan triangulation. Its coverage test is described below.

## 1. Actual family, masses, and invariant normalization

Both width and halfheight arrays in (1) are positive and sampled-concave. Their stated affine-piece interpolants therefore give a genuine convex body, with exactly the five displayed integer fibers. There is no replacement of an incompatible sampled array by its hull. Direct rational evaluation gives

    M=8140687/800000,
    V_0=20553/10000,
    Q=8130713/1600000.

The within-fiber covariance formulas have the correct rectangle factors: Var(x)=r_z^2/12 and Var(y)=H_z^2/3, weighted by area 2r_z H_z. Both diagonal entries are positive and the off-diagonal entry is zero. Thus epsilon in (3) gives exactly delta sqrt(c t^2+u^2) at the origin. The weaker rational displacement delta |u| is no larger, and is strictly smaller when t is nonzero. Reflection in x and y independently permits t,u>=0 without changing the base tilt a.

The proper-minor quota verification is complete for this one-dimensional base: its nonempty closed subsets are consecutive chains. Singletons are below M/2; a proper chain of at least two sites has both parities and mass strictly below M. All sampled fibers are positive, so this last strictness is automatic once the chain is proper. These quotas do not make the family an extremal bad family.

## 2. Actual cap polynomial and constant-status cells

For t,u>0, direct integration of a rectangle gives (7), including its factor 1/(2tu). The signs of the four corner terms are +,-,-,+. Subtracting Q therefore gives the quadratic numerator

    sum sign(l) (l_+)^2 - 2tuQ.

The symmetric matrix convention A_12=A_21=-Q is correct. Homogeneity permits t+u+|a|=1, and the two signs of a cover all oblique normals, with harmless duplicate coverage at a=0.

Independently of the clipping generator, the audit verifier checks that every saved triangle lies in this closed parameter simplex and is nondegenerate. For each of its twenty actual corner forms, all three vertex values are nonnegative or all are nonpositive. Hence the form has a fixed sign over the WHOLE triangle. Expanding the actual positive terms directly in the six quadratic power-basis monomials reproduces the saved matrix exactly. This checks the geometric status, rather than relying only on its label or a value at a sampled normal.

A nonzero homogeneous linear form cannot vanish identically on one of these nondegenerate triangles: its affine span is t+u+b=1. Forms zero only on an edge contribute zero there from either adjoining expression. Thus no supporting seam changes the polynomial value.

## 3. Independent all-normal coverage and strictness

The source's clipping algorithm is itself valid. Starting with a convex polygon, its two halfplane clips cover it, intersect only along the clipping line, and remain convex. The implementation includes zero vertices, inserts every strict edge crossing, preserves cyclic order, and discards only zero-area pieces. A zero-area discarded trace remains in the adjoining closed positive-area pieces. Since none of the twenty forms is identically zero on a two-dimensional cell, no full-dimensional cell is duplicated. A fan from a polygon vertex covers the whole convex polygon; deleting degenerate fan triangles does not remove a two-dimensional region or its closed boundary.

The independent replay uses a different proof of coverage for the final artifact. Separately for each sign of a it verifies:

1. Every triangle is contained in the parameter simplex.
2. Every pair of distinct triangles has an exact separating edge axis, so their interiors are disjoint.
3. The sum of their doubled (t,u)-areas is exactly one, the doubled area of the parameter simplex.

Consequently their finite closed union is the entire simplex. If a point of the simplex were missing, the complement of that finite closed union would contain a relative neighborhood of the point; even at an edge or vertex, that neighborhood has positive two-dimensional area in the simplex. This would contradict exact area equality. This argument checks full coverage, not merely a volume total that might hide overlap and holes. The saved labels give 54 and 56 clipping cells and 193 nondegenerate triangles in total.

The audit recomputes all six quadratic Bernstein coefficients on each triangle. They are nonnegative. It also checks every nonempty vertex subset: if all coefficients on that subset vanish, all its vertices have t=0 or all have u=0. At a zero of a nonnegative Bernstein expansion, every coefficient corresponding to the positive barycentric support must vanish. Such a point therefore lies on one of those two axes. This proves strict positivity of the actual quadratic numerator at EVERY t,u>0, including clipping seams and b=0. Hence every oblique continuous direction has captured mass strictly above Q already for the weaker displacement.

## 4. Axes, unbounded base tilts, and closed caps

The vertical-axis function is exactly the stated sum of interval clamp functions. Its complete breakpoints, including zero, are

    -8089/8000, -8031/8000, -1/2, 0,
    1999/4000, 2001/4000, 8027/8000, 8093/8000.

The unique smallest tabulated mass is Q at a=-1/2. Between consecutive breakpoints the function is affine. Both unbounded tails are constant because every nonzero-base fiber is already full or empty there; the source fiber is independent of a. The saved endpoint masses on both tails are strictly above Q. Thus there are no missing minimizers at infinity or on an untested interval. The slopes away from -1/2 are exactly 1/200 toward the left and 3/200 toward the right.

The horizontal-axis function, before its positive actual buffer is added, likewise has every clamp breakpoint included. Its minimum is exactly Q+13/20000. Therefore all horizontal actual buffered caps are strict. The pure-base closed caps through zero include the source fiber and each have mass strictly above Q. These checks include all axes where the formula with denominator 2tu is unavailable; no limiting division is used.

The minimally admissible threshold at either minimizing orientation has a proper own-fiber trace. Relaxing it strictly outward therefore adds a positive own-fiber strip. A cap with a nonminimal threshold cannot introduce a new critical cap. The only minimizing positive-normal rays are precisely those of y-z/2>=-delta and -y-z/2>=-delta.

## 5. Unique global deepestness

The four other integer bases have the exact pure-base upper bounds printed in Section 5. All are strictly below Q, uniformly over their continuous marks and independently of the buffer. No all-normal lower bound is needed at those bases.

At base zero the projective energy equals V_0 at its centroid. For any nonzero interior mark X, the derivative of the objective at the constant projective denominator in parameter direction -X is -3V_0|X|^2, so the energy is strictly below V_0. The small parameter variation is admissible on the compact rectangle. At a boundary mark the stated inward supporting denominator gives energy tending to zero by dominated convergence; its supporting face has zero planar volume. Thus the vertical displacement delta_X is strictly below delta except at the centroid.

For X=(x_0,y_0), choose the vertical sign agreeing with y_0. Its buffered cap has threshold |y_0|-delta_X, which is strictly higher than -delta unless X=0. It is a strict subset, in own-fiber volume, of the corresponding mass-Q critical cap. This proves the depth at EVERY other point of K_0 is strictly below Q, including points with y_0=0 and x_0 nonzero. Together with the all-normal source lower bound and the atomic bounds at the other bases, the origin is the unique actual global maximizer.

## 6. Inside/outside statuses and exact scope

For the plus cap, at z=-2 its boundary is y=-1-delta=-H_-2; the whole fiber is captured, with its bottom facet an inside supporting trace of length one. At z=2 its boundary is y=1-delta=H_2; only the top boundary facet is captured, giving an outside supporting trace of length 101/100. The other three fiber cuts are proper. Reflection gives the same inside/outside base sites for the minus cap.

Since Sections 2--4 exhaust all minimizing orientations, every minimizing cap at the unique global deepest point has a positive-length inside facet. This is stronger than a fixed-mark example. Its normalized depth is exactly 8130713/16281374, well above 2/9, and the source makes no joint-minimum claim. It therefore refutes unqualified inside-free critical-cap selection at a deepest buffered point, while leaving the variational bad-minimum questions open.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
